chunks: Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath, who said:

He said to me: “Do you know what was the reason for our entering into this matter and our coming to know it, while we had no mention of it with us, nor any knowledge of anything of what the people had?” He said: I said to him, “What was that?” He said: “Abū Jaʿfar — meaning Abū al-Dawānīq — said to my father Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath: ‘O Muḥammad, find for me a man of intellect who can carry out something on my behalf.’ My father said to him: ‘I have found him for you; this is so-and-so ibn Muhājir, my maternal uncle.’ He said: ‘Bring him to me.’”

He said: “So I brought my maternal uncle to him. Abū Jaʿfar said to him: ‘O Ibn Muhājir, take this wealth and go to al-Madīnah. Go to ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥasan and a number of the people of his household, among them Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and say to them: “I am a stranger from the people of Khurāsān, and there are Shiʿah there from among your Shiʿah who have sent this wealth to you.” Give to each one of them on such-and-such a condition. Then when they take the wealth, say: “I am a messenger, and I would like to have with me your written acknowledgements that you have received what you have taken.”’”

So he took the wealth and went to al-Madīnah, then returned to Abū al-Dawānīq while Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath was with him. Abū al-Dawānīq said to him: ‘What news do you bring?’ He said: ‘I went to the people, and these are their written acknowledgements of having received the wealth, except for Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad. I came to him while he was performing salat (prayer) in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, so I sat behind him and said: “When he finishes, I will mention to him what I mentioned to his companions.”’

Then he hastened and finished, then turned to me and said: ‘O you, be wary of Allah and do not deceive the Ahl al-Bayt of Muḥammad, for they are only recently removed from the rule of Banū Marwān and all of them are in need.’ So I said: ‘What is that? May Allah set you right!’ He said: ‘Then he brought his head close to me and informed me of everything that had taken place between me and you, as though he had been the third of us.’

He said: “Then Abū Jaʿfar said to him: ‘O Ibn Muhājir, know that there is no household of prophethood except that among it there is a muḥaddath, and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad is our muḥaddath today.’ This indication was the cause of our holding this doctrine.”

key_terms.أَهْلَ بَيْتِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the Household of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: How did some people come to recognize the special spiritual authority of Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report recounts how a political ruler tested members of the Prophet’s family with money, and how Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام exposed the hidden plot without being told. The narration presents this as a sign of his divinely granted knowledge and as a reason some came to recognize his special authority. It also preserves a statement about a muḥaddath being present in a household of prophethood.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Bin Al Ash’as who said,

‘He said to me: ‘Do you know what was the cause of our entry into this matter (Al-Wilayah) and our understanding with it, and what there was nothing with us from it, neither a Zikr (Mention) nor any understanding) from what was with the people’. I said, ‘What is that (cause)?’ Abu Ja’far, meaning Al-Dawaniqy said to Abu Muhammad Bin Al-Ash’as, ‘O Muhammad! Find a man for me who has intellect for him who can officiate on my behalf’. So my father said to him, ‘I have come across him for you. This is so and so Bin Muhajir, my maternal uncle’. He said, ‘So come to me with him’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went over to him with my maternal uncle. So Abu Ja’far said to him, ‘O Ibn Muhajir! Take this wealth and go to Al-Medina, and go to Abu Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan Bin Al-Hassan, and a number of his family, among them being Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, and say to them, ‘I am a stranger from the people of Khurasan, and with it a Shia from your Shias diverted me to you with this wealth’, and hand it over to each one of them upon a stipulation of such and such. So when they take possession of the wealth, so say, ‘I am a messenger and I would love it if there happens to be your letters with me of your having taken possession of whatever you have taken possession of’.

So he took the wealth and went to Al-Medina. Then he returned to Al-Dawaniqy, and Muhammad Bin Al Ash’as was in his presence. So Abu Al-Dawaniqy said to him, ‘What is behind you?’ He said, ‘I went to the group of people and these here are their letters of their having taken possession of the wealth, apart from Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws, for I went over to himasws and heasws was praying Salat in the Masjid of Rasoolsaww. So I sat (there waiting) himasws, and I said (to myself), ‘(I shall wait) until heasws finishes, then I shall mention to himasws what I mentioned to hisasws companions’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> hastened and finished, then turned around to me, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O you! Fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and do not deceive the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, for they are very close to the era of the government of Marwan, and all of them are needy’. So I said, ‘And what is that? May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> brought his<sup>asws</sup> head close to mine and informed me with the entirety of what had flowed between me and you to the extent that it was as if he<sup>asws</sup> was a third of us’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Abu Ja’far said to him, ‘O Ibn Muhajir! Know that there isn’t a Prophet-hood from the Peopleasws of the Household except and among them is a Muhaddath, and that Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws is our Muhaddath today (the one with whom the Angels speak to)’. And thus, this here is the evidence, the cause of our words (beliefs), due to this discussion’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn me has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from certain persons of his people from abu Basir who has said the following.

“I had a neighbor who followed the Sultan and he gains certain properties. He would arrange parties and invite female singers. They would drink wine and would disturb me. I complained to the man several times but he would not pay any attention. When I insisted he said, “O man, “I am an addicted man and you are sober. I wish you take me to your master and hope Allah will save me through him. His words impressed me a great deal. When I went to see abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) and mentioned the condition of the man to him. The Imam (a.s.) said, “When you will go back to Kufa he may come to you, say to him, “Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (a.s.) said to you, “Stay away from what are involved in I guarantee that Allah will admit you in Paradise.”

When returned to Kufa he came to me. I kept him with me until just two of us were let alone. I then said to him, “O man, I mentioned you to abu ‘Abdallah, Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (a.s.) and he said to me, “When you will return to al-Kufa, the man will soon come to you. Say to him, ‘Ja‘far ibn Muhammad said to you, “Stay away from what you are involved in and I will guarantee that Allah will admit you in Paradise.’”

The narrator has said that the man then wept and said to me, “I swear you to Allah, did abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) really say this to you?” The narrator has said that swore before him that abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) did really said so.”

He said, “This is enough for you and he left. After few days he called me while he was behind his house naked and said to me, “O abu Basir, by Allah, there is nothing left in my house. I gave all of them away and I am left as you see”. The narrator has said, “I then went to our people and collected for him to clothe him. Shortly afterwards he sent someone to me that he was ill and that I must see him. Thereafter I would come and go to him and provide him treatment until he was about to die. I was sitting near to him and was experiencing the agony of dieath. He fainted and then regained conscience and said to me, “O abu Basir, your master has fulfilled his promise to me.” He then passed away. May Allah grant him blessings.

When I went for Hajj I went to see abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) and asked permission for a meeting. As I was about to enter to his presence, one step in the corridor and one inside, the Imam (a.s.) before I would say anything, said from the inside, “O abu Basir, we fulfilled our promise to your friend.”
